To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a novel integrated droplet-based microdevice for controlled dosing, mixing, and incubation of pico- and nanoliter droplets and that the droplet contents were analyzed by nanoelectro-spray mass spectrometry.
we have developed a monolithic microfluidic platform that integrates all of the functions required for controlled dispensing, mixing and analysis of pico- and nanoliter-sized aqueous droplets in oil.
we have integrated a droplet-based microreactor with an integrated nanoelecrospary emitter for online mass spectrometry analysis of the contents of the droplets.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the design, fabrication and testing of a novel integrated microdevice for the controlled dispensing and mixing, as well as the incubation and extraction of pico- or nanoliter-sized aqueous droplets in oil.

the development of a microfluidic platform that is capable of performing a range of biochemical reactions and separations, and ultimately the integration of the platform with mass spectrometry for on-chip proteomic analysis.
developing a new generation of miniaturized, integrated and automated analytical devices that will enable the rapid analysis of biological samples.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we present a monolithic droplet-based microdevice that integrates droplet generation, mixing, incubation, and extraction for subsequent mass spectrometric analysis.

the integrated droplet-on- demand microfluidic platform enables accurate and precise dosing and rapid reagent mixing in pico- to nano-liter volumes, and the ability to perform online mass spectrometry analysis of these droplets.
this work presents an integrated droplet microfluidics platform that enables controlled dispensing, mixing and incubation of picoliter-sized droplet contents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the integration of all of the functional components into a monolithic device has been successfully demonstrated.
we have developed a monolithic droplet-on-demand device for controlled dosing, mixing, and analysis of picoliter to nanoliter sized droplets.
we have developed a microfluidic platform that can perform all the necessary functions for a complete mass spectrometry analysis of droplets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the droplet-based platform can be used as a tool to perform a wide range of experiments in a controlled manner, with the potential to enable a wide variety of applications.
droplet generation, mixing, incubation, extraction and analysis of pico- and nanoliter-sized samples can all be performed on a monolithic microfluidic platform.
we have developed a platform that can be used to study chemical processes at the pico- to picomolar concentration range, and to perform chemical analysis of the reaction products.
